Yes, that's the distinction I wanted, drawn clearly. In the same "•••" menu I could see two plainly different choices — "Move to Archive" for tucking something away, and "Delete permanently" set apart and marked as the serious one. Choosing delete didn't just whisk it away; it stopped me with a warning naming the bookmark and telling me this can't be undone, so I had to deliberately confirm. Only then did the CSS Grid card actually go.

That's exactly right: archiving feels safe and reversible, deleting feels weighty and final, and the confirmation makes sure I don't wipe something out by accident. The two never blur together. Happy with this — it's the "set aside versus really get rid of it" pair I had in mind.
